title: The 10 Best Tire Pressure Gauges
subtitle: Digital, dial and pencil tire pressure gauges for cars, trucks and RVs, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A good tire gauge takes the guesswork out of tire pressure, which affects grip, mileage and tire wear. We ranked 10 best-sellers from AstroAI, ETENWOLF, JACO and TIRETEK on rating, review volume and features (±1 PSI or ±1% accuracy, ANSI calibration, a bleed valve, a lit display and battery-free operation).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Geartronics Digital Tire Pressure Gauge, 150 PSI, 2-Pack
avoid.verdict: A two-pack of digital gauges whose listing never says how accurate they are, the one spec a gauge exists for.
reasons: None of the bullets or the spec table give an accuracy figure or calibration standard. Every digital gauge we ranked lists one, except the AstroAI ATG180, which at least lists resolution.
The part number field reads '150psi' and the model field is a 10-digit number, so it's hard to tell what you're buying.
It's rated 4.4 stars. The AstroAI GL-0801A costs less, states ±1 PSI, and has 72,656 reviews.

buyers_guide.a: Digital gauges are easiest to read and usually accurate to about 1 PSI. Dial gauges need no batteries and many glow in the dark. Pencil gauges are cheap glove-box backups but read to a few PSI.

buyers_guide.q: What accuracy should I look for?
buyers_guide.a: Look for a stated figure: ±1 PSI or ±1% is good. ANSI B40.1 Grade A or B40.7 Grade 2A means the gauge was calibrated to a recognized standard.
Cars run 30 to 40 PSI and spares about 60. RVs, trailers and heavy trucks can need 80 to 120 PSI or more, so pick a gauge that reads above your highest tire.
A bleeder lets you let air out a little at a time while the gauge stays on the valve, so you can hit the exact pressure.
Check cold tires, before driving or after the car has sat for a few hours. Use the pressure on the door jamb sticker, not the number on the tire sidewall.
